content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Thread Groups and Execution Order in Apache JMeter"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding how Apache JMeter handles Thread Groups and the order of execution is crucial for building accurate and reliable performance test scripts. This tutorial covers the fundamentals of Thread Groups and the exact sequence in which test elements are executed."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is a Thread Group?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Thread Group is the starting point of any JMeter test plan. Each thread represents a simulated user interacting with your application. Thread Groups allow you to control the number of users (threads), the ramp-up period (how long it takes to start all threads), and the loop count (how many times each thread executes)."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Types of Thread Groups"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Standard Thread Group: The classic and most commonly used component for simulating concurrent users."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stepping Thread Group: Allows users to ramp up incrementally in steps, useful for stress testing."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Concurrency Thread Group: Designed to target a specific concurrency model with precise arrival rates."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"JMeter Execution Order Rules"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"JMeter executes test elements based on a strict set of scoping and ordering rules. If you do not understand these rules, your samplers might execute out of expected sequence."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"1. Configuration Elements: Processed before any samplers in the same scope."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"2. Pre-Processors: Executed just before the sampler they are attached to runs."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"3. Timers: Executed before the sampler if they apply to that sampler."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"4. Samplers: The actual requests sent to the server (HTTP Request, JDBC Request, etc.)."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"5. Post-Processors: Executed immediately after the sampler completes (e.g., extracting response data with Regex)."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"6. Assertions: Processed after the Post-Processor to validate the response."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"7. Listeners: Processed last to handle data collection and reporting."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Multiple Thread Groups Execution"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, when a Test Plan contains multiple Thread Groups, JMeter executes them simultaneously (in parallel). If you need them to run sequentially (one after another), you must check the option \"Run Thread Groups consecutively\" at the Test Plan level."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"Test Plan Settings:\n[x] Run shutdown processes after each Thread Group\n[x] Run Thread Groups consecutively (i.e. one by one)"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering Thread Groups and execution order ensures that your JMeter scripts accurately mirror real-world user workflows. Always verify your element hierarchy and Test Plan settings before initiating large-scale performance tests."}]
